summary.text: Bill Hagerty is the Republican U.S. Senator from Tennessee, seeking a second term. A Vanderbilt-trained lawyer, he worked in consulting and private equity, served in the George H.W. Bush administration, and was Tennessee's commissioner of economic and community development (2011-2014) and U.S. Ambassador to Japan (2017-2019). He was first elected to the Senate in 2020.

paragraphs.text: Hagerty was born in Gallatin, Tennessee, and is originally from Sumner County. He graduated from Madisonville North Hopkins High School in Kentucky and became an Eagle Scout.
He earned a bachelor's degree from Vanderbilt University in 1981 and a law degree from Vanderbilt in 1984.

He began his business career at Boston Consulting Group, where his work took him to five continents, including three years based in Tokyo, and later became a venture capital and private equity investor, executive and board member.

According to Ballotpedia, he founded and was managing director of Hagerty Peterson & Company, worked on the domestic policy staff of the George H. W. Bush administration, was a White House fellow, and served as national finance chairman of Mitt Romney's 2008 presidential campaign.
From 2011 to 2014, Hagerty took leave from business to serve in Gov. Bill Haslam's cabinet as commissioner of the Tennessee Department of Economic and Community Development.
His official biography says he reorganized the department, eliminating more than 40 percent of its positions.
He served on Donald Trump's 2016-2017 presidential transition team, where he oversaw presidential appointments.
President Trump nominated Hagerty as U.S. Ambassador to Japan in March 2017, and the Senate confirmed him 86-12 on July 13, 2017; he announced in July 2019 that he would resign to run for the Senate.

Hagerty won the 2020 Republican primary for the open seat of retiring Sen. Lamar Alexander and defeated Democrat Marquita Bradshaw in the general election, 1,840,926 votes (62.2%) to 1,040,691 (35.2%).
He took office on January 3, 2021, and serves on the Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs, Foreign Relations, Appropriations, and Rules and Administration committees.
Wikipedia credits him with drafting the GENIUS Act, a stablecoin law signed on July 18, 2025.
He was unopposed in the August 6, 2026 Republican primary, receiving 623,538 votes.
According to his official biography, Hagerty and his wife Chrissy live in Davidson County and have four children.
